entities.name: Oral contraceptive pills
observations: Continue if satisfactory and medically appropriate; they prevent pregnancy but do not prevent gonorrhea or chlamydia.
Switching contraception is not indicated solely because of recurrent STI episodes.

entities.name: Gonorrhea and chlamydia
observations: Repeated infections are commonly reinfections rather than contraceptive failure.
A sexually active woman aged 23 should receive at least annual screening; retesting about 3 months after treatment is recommended for recurrent infection.

entities.name: Dual protection
observations: Add consistent condom use while continuing oral contraceptive pills; condoms reduce STI transmission and provide additional pregnancy protection.

entities.name: STI partner management
observations: Advise abstinence until treatment is complete and the CDC-specified post-treatment interval has passed, and ensure relevant sex partners are evaluated and treated.
Offer HIV and syphilis testing as indicated and assess HIV PrEP eligibility based on risk.
